policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere and ketiv differ only in the conjunctive waw; both read 'he shall ask/beg in harvest'. ASV's 'Therefore he shall beg in harvest' opens the clause with a discourse connective that the ASV also supplies in its margin ('Or, Therefore when he seeketh in harvest'), so 'Therefore' is the translators' English link and not a rendering that requires the waw. The one note here is classed alternative_rendering and concerns the English wording of the clause, not the reading. Nothing in the verse distinguishes the two; base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

ASV renders the plural 'that is surety for foreigners', matching the ketiv נכרים (masculine plural), and its mapped textual_variant note relegates the qere to the margin: 'Another reading is, a foreign woman' — i.e. נָכְרִיָּה, the feminine singular base candidate, is what the ASV declined in the text. Text and note together put the ketiv in the ASV's line.

בֶּאֱשׁוּן and באישון are orthographic variants of the same word for the pupil/black of darkness; they carry no difference in sense. ASV 'shall be put out in blackness of darkness' renders either identically, and the verse carries no note. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

ASV reads 'An inheritance may be gotten hastily at the beginning' — 'hastily' is the sense of the qere מְבֹהֶלֶת (root בהל, to hasten). The ketiv מבחלת is from בחל, greed or loathing, which would yield 'gotten greedily' or 'loathed'; the ASV shows no trace of that sense in the text and gives no note offering it. The wording distinguishes the qere.

The candidates differ as noun (תַּמְרוּק, a cleansing/scouring) against verb (תמריק, scours away), with the same lexical sense of cleansing in both. ASV 'Stripes that wound cleanse away evil' is an English finite verb, which renders a predicate noun in construct as readily as a finite Hebrew verb, so the clause does not discriminate the forms. No note attaches to the verse. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
